parts_and_uncertainties: Frame layout (two leaning posts, beam on top, heddle rod on brackets, shed rod): R, generic warp-weighted loom type; MC02 is a modern Bavarian museum reconstruction used only as a type comparator.
Lean 15 deg, height 1.9 m, width 1.5 m, depth 0.6 m: R/design (brief).
Cloth 0.9 m wide, tabby texture, undyed colour: R/design, not evidence of fibre, weave or colour.
Warp density: stylised (8 visible threads per bundle per layer); real warps are far denser.
18 weights in two staggered ranks, 0.105 m pitch: R/design (brief count; research elsewhere suggests 24 per household loom).
Base-down vs base-up rows: both offered; base-up follows the S-CH19 hypothesis from hole wear, base-down the museum convention.

Tie loops through the holes bear on the hole side nearest the upper end when hanging (R): in the base-up row that is the side towards the base, consistent with the reported wear in the lower part of the hole when the weight stands base-down.
Weaver position 0.7 m in front: R/design (brief); no posture or technique claimed.

incorporated_resources.what: LOOMWEIGHT-001 r001 models/loomweight.glb (this project's own earlier return, unchanged)

deviations: Three GLBs instead of the brief's two: the required loom_frame.glb and loom_weaving.glb (with row option node `weights_base_down`) plus loom_weaving_base_up.glb carrying the named option `weights_base_up`. Putting both rows in one file would overlap 36 weights at load (glTF core has no visibility flag); the manager may instead merge them and toggle the two row nodes at runtime.
Added per-row `tie_loops` meshes (1,080 triangles, cord loops through each hole) so the close-up contact reads; still inside the 2,500-triangle non-weight budget.
tools/inspect_asset.py was not run or edited (it does not know batch-5 IDs); independent measurements are in checks/.
